name: Container Coffee Shop
description:
ABOUT THE SAMAN CONTAINER COFFEE SHOP

Coffee is a workflow business, and this page sells the workflow. The building is the proven container cafe shell; what you are specifying here is everything a barista touches between order and handover: machine position, grinder circuit, water quality, waste path, display and queue. Get those right and one operator serves a rush; get them wrong and no amount of floor area saves the morning.

WHAT THE PRICE COVERS

Base specification carries the standard cafe shell plus the coffee fit-out layer: dedicated espresso and grinder circuits on the distribution board, a treated water point plumbed for the machine, under-counter waste routing, glazed display at the counter face and the branded frontage framing. The 200 sq ft shop is ₹3,70,000 ex-GST ex-factory, sharing the cafe range ladder from ₹2,03,500 through ₹6,95,600. Machines, grinders and smallwares stay your purchase; the building arrives ready to receive them.

WHY THE WATER POINT IS LISTED BEFORE THE MACHINE

Espresso equipment fails on scale before it fails on anything else, and a compact bar has no space for a spare. Plumbing treatment into the build, rather than retrofitting a filter under a finished counter, is the cheapest insurance a coffee business can buy, so it ships as part of the base fit-out on every size.

FROM WINDOW TO DESTINATION

The six sizes trace a growth path: pickup-window bars where footfall passes, split order-and-collect counters for commuter peaks, seated rooms where the brand wants guests to stay, and the 400 sq ft flagship with a retail wall. The explorer above carries the working detail per size; the full structural specification lives on the container cafe hub, linked above, because the shell is common and this page owns what is not.

ORDERING

Send the enquiry with your daily cup target and pitch details and a fixed-price quotation follows within 48 hours. Delivery runs 7 to 21 working days from confirmation. Counter length, hatch side, display extent and branding panels follow your drawing.

5-year structural warranty and 1-year finishing warranty as standard; finishing warranty extendable to 2 years on request, confirmed at quotation. Service life is 20 to 25 years under proper use and maintenance, and that is a service life, not a warranty period. Manufactured by SAMAN POS India Private Limited: ISO 9001:2015, ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 certified, NSIC and Udyam registered, 3,000+ happy customers.

mainEntity.name: Can a 10-ft container coffee shop actually run a real prosumer or commercial espresso machine, or just a domestic-grade unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The standard SAMAN MCB panel handles a single-phase 15A circuit for a prosumer machine (Rocket, Lelit, ECM grade) on its own breaker. For a commercial dual-boiler unit (La Marzocco Linea Mini Pro, Slayer single-group, Synesso), we upgrade the panel to 3-phase 20A at the order stage. Specify your machine model at quote conversation so we factory-fit the right breaker capacity before dispatch.

mainEntity.name: I want a coffee shop and I might relocate it in 2–3 years — should I buy this 10-ft coffee unit or the mobile container cafe?

acceptedAnswer.text: Depends on how many moves are in your plan. If you expect 1 relocation across the unit's life — say, a 3-year lease that may not renew — this page's coffee-fitted build is the cleaner economic call; lift points can be retrofitted at a small one-time cost and the espresso-bar fitout is preserved. If you're planning 2 or more relocations at 12-to-36 month intervals — leased plots with short tenure or brand expansion across multiple sites — start with the mobile build instead. It is engineered for the move from day one.

mainEntity.name: What's the minimum site footprint I need around the 10-ft coffee unit for queue space and outdoor seating?

acceptedAnswer.text: Plan for 100 to 250 sq ft alongside the unit for a queue line and 6 to 12 outdoor covers, scaling with how much dwell time your concept generates. Add 50 sq ft minimum behind the unit for utility access — water tank, gas cylinder if your concept needs one, MCB panel reach. Specialty coffee concepts where customers sit and read for an hour push to the 250+ sq ft end; quick takeaway-led concepts work at 100 sq ft.

mainEntity.name: Can I run a single-product non-coffee concept — juice, tea, dessert, or vada pav — in the same 10-ft container coffee shop unit?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — the espresso bar fitout adapts to other single-product menus. A juice bar omits the boiler line and adds a blender circuit. A tea brand kiosk swaps the espresso machine for kettle-grade electrical, with the grinder removed. A dessert or vada pav counter replaces the milk fridge cutout with a chiller cutout and adjusts the exhaust hood for the cooking load. Specify the menu at order so the factory-fit matches before dispatch — converting after delivery is more expensive than ordering it right.

mainEntity.name: What does the inside look like before I add my own coffee machine, grinder, and fridge — is it factory-fitted or just a bare steel shell?

acceptedAnswer.text: Factory-fitted. The espresso bar wall arrives with the work surface, sink, grinder pad, milk fridge cutout, syrup rail, and exhaust micro-hood opening already in place. The customer window is cut and shuttered. The MCB panel is wired with labelled circuits. The exterior is painted in your brand colour. What you add: the espresso machine, the grinder, the milk fridge, the water boiler, signage, furniture. Marketplace listings advertising "container coffee shop" at ₹90,000 to ₹1,60,000 are bare steel shells without any of this fit-out — that is the difference.
